statement: 韩国计划提高加拿大原油进口，以分散中东供应风险。韩国贸易部称，2026年目标进口加拿大原油最高1600万桶，较2025年488万桶大幅增加，并研究进一步提升至2000万桶/年。韩国炼厂希望用 Cold Lake、Access Western Blend 等加拿大重/中质酸油优化原料池，降低对中东供应风险的暴露。

statement: 挪威 Hammerfest LNG 于6月8日开始计划检修，预计至6月11日初结束。该装置技术处理能力为1840万立方米/日。检修发生在全球 LNG 供应偏紧背景下，欧洲买家近期难以与亚洲高价市场竞争现货船货。2026年至今 Hammerfest 已出口约220万吨 LNG，其中约210万吨流向欧洲。

statement: Goldman Sachs estimated April 2026 global oil demand destruction at 4-5 mb/d, or about 4-5% versus a no-war counterfactual, attributing the shock to Hormuz-related disruption.

value.counterfactual: no-war global demand growth at annualized 1 mb/d pace

methodology: Goldman triangulates across refinery runs/product stocks, high-frequency demand plus retail fuel prices, and estimates from other forecasters/trading houses. Keep as institution view, not merged actual demand.

provenance.quote: 4-5mb/d of global oil demand destruction in April

statement: Goldman's refinery-runs-and-product-stocks method implied just under 4 mb/d of April 2026 global oil demand destruction after including an estimated 2 mb/d hit to non-refined demand such as LPG and ethane petrochemical feedstocks.
methodology: Estimate apparent refined product demand from refinery runs minus product inventory draws, then add non-refined demand decline based on LPG and ethane demand in IEA and S&P Global May balances.

provenance.section: Approach 1: Using Refinery Runs and Product Stocks

statement: Goldman's high-frequency demand and retail-price method estimated just over 5 mb/d of April 2026 global oil demand destruction, with weak China gasoline-related sales, soft Western Europe demand, and solid US gasoline nowcast as key inputs.

demandSignals.China: very weak gasoline and related products retail sales

methodology: Combine high-frequency demand measures for gasoline in China, US, Europe and India plus European diesel with retail gasoline price changes and an estimated gasoline elasticity of -0.25; use IEA, S&P Global and Wood Mackenzie averages for other products.

provenance.quote: just over 5mb/d of global oil demand destruction

statement: Goldman estimated China April 2026 gasoline and related products retail sales volumes fell just over 20% year on year.
methodology: Goldman estimate based on Wind and NBS data in Exhibit 3; preserve as Goldman estimate because underlying retail series is not separately stored here.

statement: Pre-war (Feb 2026): ~135 vessels/day, including ~54 oil/chemical/LPG tankers and ~6 LNG carriers transited Strait of Hormuz daily. ~20 mb/d crude and products (~20% of global supply), plus ~30% of LPG, ~20% of LNG, ~16% of alumina, ~14% of fertilizers.
source: S&P Global Energy / Commodities at Sea (CAS)
methodology: S&P Global Commodities at Sea (CAS) and MINT data

statement: By late May 2026, total Strait traffic collapsed to avg 11 vessels/day, <2 tankers/day - more than 90% below pre-conflict norms. March: 7 vessels/day. April: fragile recovery to 14/day (4 tankers). US-sanctioned vessels: 45% of March transits, 29% in April.
source: S&P Global Energy / Commodities at Sea (CAS)
methodology: S&P Global CAS and MINT data

statement: Mid-April 2026: US blockade in Gulf of Oman targeting Iranian-linked vessels. In first month, 30-40 vessels crossed blockade line daily, only small fraction successfully transited Strait. 14 vessels recorded turned back. No Iranian crude tankers confirmed through both Strait and blockade since mid-April.
source: S&P Global Energy / Commodities at Sea (CAS)

scope.geography: Gulf of Oman / Strait of Hormuz

methodology: CAS data, MINT data

statement: War risk premiums for Strait transit surged 1000%+. Pre-war: 0.1-0.3% of hull value. Post-attacks: 2.5-5%. For VLCC (00-150M): .5-7.5M per voyage. MR tanker AWRP: 0-120k for 7 days. By late March eased to 0.8-1.5% but remain significantly above pre-war.
methodology: Market participant feedback to Platts

statement: More than 800 laden vessels remain stranded in Middle East Gulf. At 50% traffic rate (68 daily exits), MEG clear in ~2 weeks. At 10% (14/day), 8-9 weeks for full clearance. Assumes de-mining, insurer confidence, US-Iran cooperation.
source: S&P Global Energy / Commodities at Sea (CAS)
methodology: CAS clearance scenario modeling

statement: Multiple short-lived "open" windows undermined confidence: sub-24-hour post-ceasefire period and ~48-hour US-protected corridor were immediately followed by renewed attacks, creating a credibility gap. Behavioral drag expected: shipowners/charterers/insurers will adopt cautious wait-and-see approach.
methodology: Market participant feedback

statement: Most vessels have abandoned traditional Traffic Separation Scheme, using non-standard route through Iranian territorial waters to avoid naval mines. Only 2 vessels sailed via Oman route in first half of May. "Other" vessel types (landing craft, tugs, cargo ships, aggregate carriers) accounted for >50% of May traffic - significant shift in vessel type composition.
methodology: CAS data

statement: SOH normally transits ~15 M BPD crude (18% of 85 M BPD global) + ~5 M BPD refined products (25% of 16 M BPD waterborne exports). Post-conflict: ~1.5 M BPD transits, leaving 13.5 M BPD deficit.
methodology: Kpler/Vortexa/IEA/EIA data

statement: Three pipeline systems bypass SOH: Saudi E-W (5-7 M BPD, surged from 2.5 to 6 M BPD), UAE ADCOP (1.5-1.8 M BPD, from 1.0 to 1.5 M BPD), Kirkuk-Ceyhan (+200-250 K BPD). Combined reroute 6.7 M BPD capacity, diverted ~4 M BPD.
methodology: IEA, Macquarie Macro Strategy

statement: Global SPR release max 3.5 M BPD (avg 2 M BPD 3/16-4/30). US: 1.4 M BPD. Europe product-heavy. China unlikely to release. IEA 426M barrel plan (301M crude, 125M products). Global crude SPR 1.6B barrels; US 420M, China 1B.
methodology: IEA, Macquarie Macro Strategy

statement: Brent floor 5-90 with drift back to 10 until SOH restored. If shut until end-April: Brent 50/BBL, products 200%+ above pre-war levels. Long War: product margins $100-150, finished products 200-300% above pre-war.
methodology: Macquarie Macro Strategy modeling

statement: Asia refinery run cuts max 3.5 M BPD. China SOE: 1 M BPD. India: 300 K BPD (modest, sustained LPG output). SE Asia: 1.2 M BPD. Pengerang fully shut 300K CDU March 12. Japan/SK have flexibility.
methodology: IEA, IIR, Macquarie Macro Strategy

statement: Excluding stranded ME floating storage: ~75M barrels in floating storage globally. ~45M non-Iranian barrels eligible to discharge at large premiums. Iranian barrels may discharge if US lenient on sanctions enforcement.
methodology: Kpler, Vortexa

statement: Base case (ceasefire end-March): global loadings bottom at 29.7 M BPD (3/16), recover to 45 M BPD by early May, back to pre-war by May 4. Detailed weekly loading table by region.
methodology: Kpler/Bloomberg/IEA/EIA/Vortexa/Macquarie Modeling

statement: Long War scenario (ceasefire end-April): Hormuz loadings fall to 0 by early April. Global loadings bottom at 35.8 M BPD (5/4). Deficit persists >7 M BPD into early May. Slow recovery to near normal by late May.
methodology: Macquarie Macro Strategy

statement: Diesel crack outperformed gasoline since war start. Jet crack signaled extreme supply tensions. Middle Eastern benchmarks directly reflected AG crude transport challenges. Brent area grade differentials found support.
methodology: Bloomberg, Platts
